description: Frog becomes a story detective: Robo reads Turtle's Windy Day, then the detectives answer who, where, what happened and how they felt, prove each answer by looking back in the story, spot details that are not in the story, and solve Squirrel's Acorn on their own.

youtube.title: Story Detectives! Who, Where, What Happened | Reading for Kids | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Frog gets a detective badge! Robo reads Turtle's Windy Day, then the detectives solve the case with four clue cards: who is in the story (the characters), where it happens (the setting), what happened, and how the characters feel. Kids prove every answer by looking back in the story, learn to say "Not in the story!" when Frog invents a dragon, and solve a second story, Squirrel's Acorn, on their own.

For first graders (CCSS RL.1.1, RL.1.3).

Try at home: with a grown-up, draw four clue cards (a face, a house, a star and a heart). Read a picture book together, then answer each card and open the book to the page that proves it.

objects.text: The wind blew the hat into a tree. Squirrel got it.
Turtle had a new red hat. He walked to the pond to show his friends. Then a big wind blew. Whoosh! The red hat flew up into a tall tree.

Turtle looked up. He felt sad. "I can't climb trees," he said. Squirrel saw the hat. She ran up the tree, quick as a flash. She brought the red hat down. Turtle smiled a big smile. "Thank you, Squirrel!" he said.

Squirrel sat on a log by the pond. She had a big acorn for lunch. Plop! The acorn fell into the water. Squirrel felt worried. She did not want to get wet. Turtle swam out to the acorn. He carried it back on his shell. Squirrel clapped. "Thank you, Turtle!" she said.

do.text: Story Detectives
Frog, here's your detective badge!
A real badge? I'm a detective!
A story is full of clues. Here are four.
Who? Where? What happened? And feelings.
Watch closely, detectives. After the story, we solve the case!
A red hat! Our first clue?
Turtle's Windy Day
Turtle had a new red hat.
Look at my new red hat!
He walked to the pond to show his friends.
Hello, Turtle! What a nice hat!
Thank you! It is new.
Then a big wind blew. Whoosh!
The red hat flew up into a tall tree.
Oh no! My hat!
Turtle looked up. He felt sad.
Stretch... stretch... I can not reach it.
I can't climb trees.
I can climb trees! I will help you.
Squirrel saw the hat.
She ran up the tree, quick as a flash.
Got it!
She brought the red hat down.
Here is your hat, Turtle!
Turtle smiled a big smile.
Thank you, Squirrel!
You're welcome, Turtle!
Let's play by the pond!
The end.
Time to solve the case! Clue one: who?
Who is in the story?
Turtle and Squirrel!
The people or animals in a story are the characters.
characters
Who is the story mostly about?
Turtle! It's his hat and his windy day.
Look back!

do.words: Turtle had a new red hat

do.text: Look back. The story starts with Turtle.
Clue two: where does the story happen?
By the pond!
What clues show it? Water...
...reeds, and a tall tree.
Where a story happens is called the setting.
setting
The setting is the pond. Got it!
Clue three: what happened?
The wind blew Turtle's hat into a tree!
Yes! And how did it end?
Squirrel climbed up and brought it down.
Now a detail. What color was the hat?
Look back!

do.words: The red hat flew up into a tall tree

do.text: Red! The story says red hat.
And then a big dragon took the hat!
Hmm. Was there a dragon in the story?
No! Not in the story!
Not in the story!
A detective only uses what the story shows.
Oops. No dragons. Only true clues.
Clue four: how did Turtle feel?
At the start, with his new hat?
Happy! Look at his smile.
When his hat was stuck in the tree?
Sad. His face looks sad.
Look back!
And his words were a clue too.
At the end? He smiled and said thank you.
Happy and thankful!
Show the feelings on your face! Happy, sad, happy!
Who, where, what, feel! Look back, find the clue!
In the story, or not in the story?
The hat was red.
In the story!
Turtle could fly.
Not in the story!
Squirrel climbed the tree.
In the story!
A dragon took the hat.
Not in the story!
Squirrel's Acorn
Your turn, detectives. Listen closely.
Squirrel sat on a log by the pond.
She had a big acorn for lunch.
Plop! The acorn fell into the water.
Oh no! My acorn!
Squirrel felt worried. She did not want to get wet.
I can swim. I will get it!
Turtle swam out to the acorn.
He carried it back on his shell.
Squirrel clapped.
Thank you, Turtle!
Who? Where? What happened? Feelings? You try!
I found a clue first! Look!
Squirrel felt worried. She didn't want to get wet!
Look back!
Great detective work, Frog! You proved it.
Squirrels bury nuts and find many of them by smell.
Quiz time! In Turtle's Windy Day, who lost a hat?
Question 1
Turtle!
What color was the hat?
Question 2
Red!
Where did the hat land?
Question 3
In a tall tree!
How did Turtle feel when he couldn't reach it?
Question 4
Sad! He said, I can't climb trees.
In Squirrel's Acorn, who helped, and how?
Question 5
Turtle! He carried my acorn on his shell.
Case closed! You found every clue.
Detectives ask who, where, what happened, and how they feel.
And they look back in the story to check.
Look back, look back, find the clue! Bye!
